sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Hengelo is extending paid parking outward as the Hart van Zuid district is built. The college decided in September 2024 to introduce paid parking in the ring around Hart van Zuid north of the Esrein, phased per sub-area as housing is completed and with the blue zone kept in the shopping area; after a six-week inspection about 2,800 addresses had been written to and 160 written responses came in [6]. The first sub-area was De Clercqdwarsstraat, from 1 January 2025 [7]. For 2026 the Uitwerkingsbesluit defines six permit areas, paid Monday to Wednesday and Friday from 09:00 to 18:00, Thursday until 21:00 and Saturday until 17:00, with no visitor permits in areas 1 to 3 [10]. Addresses in the inner city and Hart van Zuid with a building permit granted after 29 September 2021 get no resident or visitor permit [10]. The college also sent the 2026 parking ordinance to the council in September 2025 proposing to remove the special charging permit, and it decided that nobody with parking on their own land gets a first resident permit [8]. The policy rests on a council decision of 2021 that set lower parking standards for the inner city and Hart van Zuid, at least 1,500 homes by 2030, with parking regulation as a condition [6]. The 2019 Parkeerplan was adopted with three measures: Shop & Go, aligned paid hours and friendly enforcement [2], but Shop & Go ended, because its technology was not suitable for enforcement, and from January 2024 its 13 spaces became blue-zone spaces with a 30-minute maximum [4][5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The Masterplan Lange Wemen was approved unanimously by the council on 17 December 2025 and the college signed an agreement with VanWonen after a decision of 26 May 2026. It provides about 310 homes and a public garage for about 430 cars plus 500 to 750 bicycle spaces, replacing the Thiemsbrug garage, and construction of the first block was expected to start at the end of 2027 [17]. The 2019 Parkeerplan had expected ground-level capacity to fall by 254 spaces by 2023 because of developments, and prepared a temporary lot at Kloosterhof of more than 100 spaces [1]. On charging, the municipality tries to place a public charger within 250 metres of every resident without parking of their own, and Vattenfall assesses requests and manages the chargers, with two spaces reserved per charger [16].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality runs garage De Beurs, at 0.50 euro per 14 minutes and 11.10 euros per 24 hours; the other facilities are the garages Thiemsbrug and De Brink and the Q-Park P+R Station Hengelo, and there are more than 900 street spaces and 13 blue-zone spaces [11]. The street and day-car-park tariff is 1.00 euro per 27 minutes for 2026, with a day maximum of 8.80 euros at the five day car parks, and a centre resident permit costs 158.20 euros a year [9]; the general centre permit costs 72.40 euros a month and the day-car-park permit 173.50 euros a year [13]. A booklet for the Lambertuskermis lists Thiemsbrug at 1.80 euros an hour and De Brink at 1.00 euro per 22 minutes, but we did not check these against operator pages [12]. De Beurs uses licence-plate recognition and is open 24 hours with a maximum height of 2.00 m [14]. The national register lists the P+R at Gieskesstraat with 270 spaces, operated by Nederlandse Spoorwegen, in an entry from 2021 that is probably out of date; we assume it is the same site as the Q-Park P+R [15]. A 2019 survey found the spaces around the centre on average about 50 percent occupied, about 40 percent on weekday daytimes and 58 to 60 percent on Saturday afternoons, and the garages together 38 percent at their busiest, with 835 spaces free; these are 2019 figures that cover the street and open lots, with the garages reported separately [0].

Our data cover the P+R Industrieplein, for about 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 11% on weekdays and 9% at weekends, with a peak of 61% on a Friday evening. The garages in the centre are not in our data.
